plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful deciduous tree that produces clouds of delicate, fragrant, almond-scented blossoms before its leaves emerge. It is among the most widely planted ornamental cherries and the centerpiece of hanami celebrations.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate parks and gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Japan's Meteorological Agency tracks the 'cherry blossom front' as it moves northward, and peak bloom at any location lasts only about one week.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy perennial bulb with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers and gray-green strap-like leaves. It naturalizes readily in woodlands and meadows and is the ancestor of many garden daffodil cultivars.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to mid-spring (March to April)
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the UK, France, and Belgium; widely cultivated in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain lycorine and other alkaloids, so the plant is toxic, and a compound from daffodils, galantamine, is used in medication for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small understory tree whose bare branches and even trunk are covered in clusters of magenta-pink pea-like flowers before heart-shaped leaves appear. It is a valuable early nectar source for native bees.
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, northern Mexico
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a slightly tangy flavor, and the flowers grow directly from old wood in a phenomenon called cauliflory.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting streets and lawns with fallen petals. In some regions it blooms in autumn or spring depending on local climate.
plants.bloomingSeason: Sporadic autumn blooms in the Southern Hemisphere; spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (starting around April in warm areas)
plants.location: Native to South America; cultivated in South Africa, Australia, Mexico, and southern California
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the 'Jacaranda City,' tens of thousands of jacaranda trees line the streets, and in Mexico City their bloom is celebrated each spring.
